standard.title: Managing changes and transitions including puberty
standard.description: investigate resources and strategies to manage changes and transitions, including changes associated with puberty
standard.prior_knowledge: At Years 3-4, students planned, rehearsed and reflected on strategies to cope with different changes and transitions they experience (AC9HP4P02). They have experience with strategies for change at a general level. This descriptor specifically includes puberty as a named change type, representing a significant new content area.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate a range of resources and strategies to manage changes and transitions, including the physical and social changes associated with puberty.

nodes.label: Understanding puberty as a change and transition
nodes.description: Describe the physical and social changes associated with puberty, understanding that experiences differ and are connected to developmental and cultural contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe at least three physical changes associated with puberty and explain that puberty experiences differ between individuals.
success_criteria: Describes changes accurately and without unnecessary value judgement
Acknowledges that timing, experience and expression of puberty varies between individuals
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who lack accurate, non-stigmatising understanding of puberty cannot engage with strategies to manage it or with the resources available. Misconceptions or shame-laden framings at this node will undermine every subsequent node in this descriptor and adjacent descriptors about consent and relationships.
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Puberty in cultural context — including First Nations Australian rites of passage and developmental ceremonies, and how different families and cultural groups acknowledge developmental change — provides rich, respectful breadth beyond the biological.

response_modes.reason: Accurate, calm, normalising presentation of puberty information. Students need to develop fluency with the vocabulary and concepts in a low-stakes environment before engaging with management strategies. Misconceptions should be addressed here, not later.

Examine puberty in diverse cultural contexts: First Nations Australian rites of passage connected to puberty; how different families acknowledge developmental stages; the range of products and resources available for managing physical changes. Cultural breadth normalises diversity of experience.

nodes.label: Identifying resources and strategies
nodes.description: Investigate the range of resources and strategies available for managing puberty changes — physical products, support people, information sources, and social strategies for managing changing roles and responsibilities.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two types of resources or strategies available for managing puberty changes, and explain the purpose of each.
success_criteria: Identifies resources across more than one type (physical products AND social/support resources)
Can explain the purpose of each resource in terms of what aspect of the change it addresses

response_modes.reason: Survey resource types: physical products for managing menstruation and other changes; trusted support people; reliable information sources; strategies for managing changing social roles and responsibilities. Breadth across resource types ensures students aren't left with only one type of management strategy.

nodes.label: Personalising strategies for managing transitions
nodes.description: Connect resource and strategy knowledge to the personal — understanding that choices are personal and preparing to make informed, autonomous choices about managing their own changes and transitions.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe how a person might make choices about resources and strategies for managing puberty changes, acknowledging that these choices are personal and may differ between individuals.
success_criteria: Acknowledges personal choice and individual difference without prescribing a single approach
Can identify at least one factor that might influence which resources or strategies a person chooses

response_modes.reason: Connects understanding of puberty changes, available resources, and the principle of personal agency into a coherent framework for managing transitions. Integrates the physical, social and cultural dimensions addressed across the nodes.
